bug_semantics: Before 2.54.0, the Team API mutation endpoints authorized with IsGranted('edit_team') and no Team subject. TeamVoter only supports the entity attributes view, edit, and delete, so it abstained; RolePermissionVoter accepted the subjectless registered edit_team permission. A lower-privilege user granted edit_team could therefore modify membership and customer, project, or activity associations of a team they neither administered nor led.
flaw_origin: 836a530b8615249ad8854fb5e8a36c08e6cdcd16 first added the Team API mutation methods for members, customers, and projects with the subjectless edit_team authorization; its immediate parent a31e027c5426ff645d43ef6307b4bc27cfa9937e contains none of those methods. 0914ebf737dd9f6acc02343cb02d9d8cfe50676e later extended the same flawed pattern to the two activity-association endpoints. b2d3272151523106027da1d31311bf6fbaf4c7d4 subsequently added the intended admin-or-teamlead object check to TeamVoter, while the API's subjectless checks continued to bypass that voter. Later annotation/attribute conversions preserved the mechanism and are refactors, not the original BIC.

ai_marker.basis: The BIC is a GitHub-signed 2020 commit authored by maintainer Kevin Papst. Its commit object and message contain no AI, bot, generated-code, or co-author marker; the bundle's repository-level AI scan signal is not evidence on this BIC.

evidence: The live GitHub advisory GHSA-jv9x-w4gm-hwcm describes the subjectless edit_team check, lists versions < 2.54.0 as affected and 2.54.0 as first patched, and is not withdrawn; the CVE.org record for CVE-2026-41498 is PUBLISHED and gives the same boundary.

In BIC 836a530b8615249ad8854fb5e8a36c08e6cdcd16, src/API/TeamController.php adds member, customer, and project mutation endpoints guarded by is_granted('edit_team'); immediate parent a31e027c5426ff645d43ef6307b4bc27cfa9937e has none of those methods. Tag 1.8 is the earliest repository tag containing this BIC.
Commit 0914ebf737dd9f6acc02343cb02d9d8cfe50676e adds the two activity-association endpoints with the same edit_team guard; tag 1.10 is the earliest tag containing that extension.

Commit b2d3272151523106027da1d31311bf6fbaf4c7d4 makes TeamVoter reject edit/delete unless the user is an admin, super-admin, or teamlead of the subject; tag 1.15 is the earliest tag containing that intended object-level restriction.

At vulnerable parent 999d820d4ca1fb3bb83395ad9bfc73d73b5eb04a (tag 2.53.0), TeamVoter supports only view/edit/delete on a Team, while RolePermissionVoter handles subjectless registered permissions; TeamController still has subjectless edit_team on the eight association endpoints (and patchAction).

Direct fix cbdf91f316ba9f4ab530127ad19b38fba4df8b0e changes each affected Team API guard from IsGranted('edit_team') to IsGranted('edit', 'team'). It is a descendant of the BIC, its sole parent is the vulnerable 2.53.0 commit, and release commit d456cd3ce2ec5d2599d6cce9490f01f67332d77f tagged 2.54.0 contains the fix.

The BIC commit object has one parent, human maintainer author Kevin Papst, GitHub committer/signature, date 2020-01-28, and message 'API methods to handle teams and users (#1384)' with no AI marker or AI co-author trailer. No finer public member commit is present in the supplied clone.
reasoning: This is a real missing object-level authorization vulnerability, not a withdrawn or rejected advisory. The earliest surviving commit that wrote the flawed Team API authorization pattern is 836a530b8615249ad8854fb5e8a36c08e6cdcd16; the activity endpoints were a later same-mechanism extension, and later syntax conversions do not replace the BIC. The direct fix supplies the Team subject so TeamVoter enforces ownership. Because AI attribution is judged only on the BIC and that signed 2020 human-authored commit has no AI marker, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
